theme: Where files live: Application Support, Caches and backups

terms.definition: The folder where your app stores important files it needs, which users never see.
terms.example: Save the notes file in the application support directory.

terms.definition: The folder for files you can download or build again, which the system may delete when space is low.
terms.example: Put the thumbnails in the caches directory.

terms.definition: A flag on a file that tells the system not to copy it into the device backup.
terms.example: Use backup exclusion for files you can download again.

video.description:
Learn to explain how to choose the right folder for app files: Application Support Directory, Caches Directory & Backup Exclusion, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Application Support Directory - The folder where your app stores important files it needs, which users never see.
Caches Directory - The folder for files you can download or build again, which the system may delete when space is low.
Backup Exclusion - A flag on a file that tells the system not to copy it into the device backup.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Application Support Directory, Caches Directory & Backup Exclusion in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Application Support Directory, Caches Directory, Backup Exclusion 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Application Support Directory - The folder where your app stores important files it needs, which users never see.
한국어: Application Support Directory: 앱이 필요로 하는 중요한 파일을 저장하는, 사용자에게 보이지 않는 폴더

Caches Directory - The folder for files you can download or build again, which the system may delete when space is low.
한국어: Caches Directory: 다시 받거나 만들 수 있는 파일을 두는 폴더로, 저장 공간이 부족하면 시스템이 지울 수 있다

Backup Exclusion - A flag on a file that tells the system not to copy it into the device backup.
한국어: Backup Exclusion: 시스템이 파일을 기기 백업에 복사하지 않도록 알려 주는 파일의 표시

In this video, Mina and Jake talk about which folder is right for notes, thumbnails and reports, and what goes in the backup, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Application Support Directory, Caches Directory and Backup Exclusion in English?

dialogue.title: Which folder is safe?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, where should I save the user's notes file?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In the application support directory. It holds files the app needs, and users never see them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Put those in the caches directory. The caches directory is for files you can download again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What happens when the phone is almost full?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The system may delete files in the caches directory, so never store user data there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay. In our code, `file` goes to `.cachesDirectory`, so it must be a thumbnail.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. The exported report goes in the application support directory. Do we back it up?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, use backup exclusion. The system then does not copy that file into the backup.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is backup exclusion good for the notes file?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. Use backup exclusion only for files you can rebuild or download again.
Save notes in the application support directory.
